title: Stable three-dimensional lattice solitons in spin-orbit-coupled Bose-Einstein condensates
authors: Liangwei Zeng, Boris A. Malomed, Yaroslav V. Kartashov, Xing Zhu
abstract: We address three-dimensional (3D) solitons maintained by spin-orbit coupling (SOC) in the binary self-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) held in the 3D optical lattice (OL). The analysis reveals that the SOC-OL interplay results in the formation of stable full-vortex (FV) soli-tons, built as sets of four density peaks residing in neighboring wells of the lattice potential, with the superimposed global vortical phase, and site-centered semi-vortices (SV), in which the vorticity is present in only one component. The full-vortex solitons, with their specific phase textures, do not exist in a uniform BEC with SOC. Full-vortex and semi-vortex states in the binary self-attractive BEC are stable despite the possibility of the supercritical collapse in the 3D system. Such states also exist, as gap solitons, in the self-repulsive 3D system. In terms of the chemical potential and number of particles, the stability regions of the 3D full-vortex solitons and semi-vortices expand with the increase of the SOC strength and OL depth. The results open the route to the creation of 3D complexes of vorticity-carrying condensates that can be realized with existing experimental techniques.
summary: This paper theoretically investigates stable three-dimensional lattice solitons in a Bose-Einstein condensate modified by spin-orbit coupling and confined in an optical lattice. The research finds that the SOC-lattice interaction stabilizes unique full-vortex and semi-vortex states, which are robust against collapse. These findings pave the way for experimentally realizing complex, vorticity-carrying quantum matter structures.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence and stability of three-dimensional (3D) lattice solitons in a binary self-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) subjected to spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
main_result: The interplay between SOC and the optical lattice (OL) stabilizes full-vortex (FV) and semi-vortex (SV) solitons, which are stable even in the presence of supercritical collapse possibilities.
method: Theoretical analysis was performed to model the soliton formation and stability within the specified quantum gas system.
model_or_system: The system is a binary self-interacting Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) confined in a 3D optical lattice (OL) and incorporating spin-orbit coupling (SOC).
key_observables: Stability regions of the 3D full-vortex solitons and semi-vortices, and the formation of density peaks and vortical phases.
important_parameters: SOC strength and OL depth, which are shown to expand the stability regions.
main_assumptions: The analysis is based on the BEC being held in a 3D optical lattice and considering the effects of SOC.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the formation and stability of 3D solitons, contrasting their existence in uniform vs. lattice potentials, and examining the stability regions for different interaction types (self-attractive vs. self-repulsive).
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the complex interplay between external potentials (OL), internal interactions (self-interaction), and spin-orbit coupling in BECs, leading to novel, stable topological structures (vortices) that are highly relevant for controlling quantum matter.
